text:
Calgary played the better game and lost it. The Flames won the share of simulated replays 59 percent to 41, outshot Anaheim 70 to 56 in attempts, and won the even-strength chance battle 2.46 expected goals to 2.08. Dustin Wolf allowed 4 goals on 2.45 expected, and the Ducks cashed in on a night when their goalie, Ville Husso, was a little better than average, stopping 27 of 29 against 2.94 expected.

The goals tell the story of a tight game that broke late. Jackson LaCombe put ANA ahead on a first-period power play, Morgan Frost tied it, and Frank Vatrano deflected one in with 45 seconds left in the period for a 2-1 lead. Aydar Suniev tied it at 2-2 late in the second on a 5 percent chance, the least likely goal of the night. Calgary's best look, a 24 percent chance for Ryan Strome in that same period, went into Husso's pads instead.

The third period decided it, and it was the one stretch where Anaheim clearly had the better of the play, 2.0 expected goals to 1.0. Ryan Poehling put ANA ahead 3-2 shorthanded at 5:35, and Nikita Nesterenko poked in the fourth goal with under three minutes left, with Mikael Granlund and Alex Killorn on the ice for stronger shot-quality numbers than anyone else up front. Calgary went 0 for 3 on the power play while ANA scored on 1 of 2, and the shorthanded goal swung the game on a night the Flames otherwise controlled.
